title: [Engine] dsv41 0.1.51: decode on fresh prompts waits on serial store reads (disk queue < 0.4 on a 990 Pro); DS4_AHEAD=1 is 10% slower (RTX 5090, Windows)
body:
All numbers measured on my machine unless marked "derived" (computed from measured counters).

## Setup
- Strata 0.2.6 / Control 0.1.51, engine `strata-dsv41` 0.1.51, build `562a0c2ed716+dsv41+cuda13.0`, NVIDIA driver 617.42, Windows 11.
- Hardware:
  - RTX 5090 32 GB, PCIe 4.0 x16 (board limit).
  - Ryzen 7 7800X3D.
  - 128 GB DDR5 (4 × 32 GB at 3600 MT/s).
  - Samsung 990 Pro 2 TB, PCIe 4.0 x4 (behind the B650 chipset), model on this drive.
- Model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, pack `ist-das-2.25bpw`, context 256k.
- Launch: `--set reserve-mib=8192 --set ssd-cache=96 --speed faster` (experts 5).
- Engine log at start:
  - `RAM store: up to 8436 slots of 11.4 MB (96.0 GB), policy 0, 8 reader threads, unbuffered reads`
  - `RAM store: 8180 of the profile's hottest experts read in (74.8 GB) in 12.8 s`
  - `13906 routed experts on the CPU lane (135.3 GB, in place in the model's files), 8 threads`
  - `CUDA0 … experts 14.53 GB (1454 of 15360 in VRAM)`

## Observation
On repeated prompts decode runs at about 25 tok/s; on never-seen prompts it drops to about 15 tok/s. That second case is what an agent workload (Hermes) actually sees. During the slow case the SSD is far from busy.

Method:
- Windows PhysicalDisk counters for the model drive, sampled every 0.7 s.
- Each phase uses only the samples inside its own requests' time window.
- Two baseline runs (A1, A2), each a fresh launch with the same expert profile file.
- Same prompts, temperature 0, no reasoning, 256 tokens per request.

| Phase | Decode tok/s | Disk read MB/s (mean) | Peak MB/s | Reads/s | KB/read | Disk queue | MB read per token (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repeated prompts, A1 | 25.0 | 222 | 640 | 497 | 1552 | 0.04 | 8.9 |
| Repeated prompts, A2 | 24.9 | 270 | 1060 | 529 | 1401 | 0.12 | 10.9 |
| Fresh prompts, A1 | 15.1 | 739 | 3869 | 861 | 957 | 0.38 | 49.0 |
| Fresh prompts, A2 | 16.1 | 764 | 1320 | 870 | 973 | 0.26 | 47.3 |
| Store preload at start (25/10 run) | — | 4300 (avg) | 5900 | — | 2900 | 1.8 | — |

### Derived
- **Per-read service time.** By Little's law (time per read = queue ÷ reads per second), fresh-prompt reads take about 0.30–0.44 ms each for about 1 MB. So roughly one read is in flight at a time.
- **Data per token.** About 48 MB per token is read from the SSD on fresh prompts, about 5 experts' worth at about 9.7 MB each.
- **Time per token.** Fresh decode costs about 64 ms per token against about 40 ms on repeated prompts, so about 24 ms more. About 50 reads of about 1 MB at 0.3–0.44 ms each, one after another, is about 15–22 ms. That is most of the gap.
- **Unused headroom.** The same drive delivers 4.3 GB/s average (5.9 GB/s peak) at queue depth 1.8 during the store preload, against 0.74–0.76 GB/s during fresh decode.

## What is not the limit (measured)
- **RAM bandwidth.**
  - A C# probe (built-in .NET, 4 GB buffer, engine stopped) reads 48–51 GB/s, against 57.6 GB/s theoretical at 3600 MT/s dual channel. Random latency is 104 ns (4 KB pages).
  - On cached decode, a 2-thread memory-read load (38 GB/s) cost about 21%, while a 2-thread CPU-only load cost about 1%. So cached decode is partly RAM-sensitive.
  - Fresh-prompt decode is dominated by the SSD wait above.
- **PCIe 4.0 x16 (GPU).** `nvidia-smi dmon` during decode: host→GPU 0.33 GB/s mean (1.3 GB/s peak), about 1–4% of the link, warm and fresh alike. Only a 13.7k-token prompt read uses it heavily: 13.3 GB/s mean, peaks 26–33 GB/s.
- **GPU power.** Power limit 400 W: decode draws 142–171 W at 2931 MHz, with no power, thermal or hardware throttling.
- **More store reader threads.** With queue < 0.4 the 8 store readers are mostly idle. I did not test `DS4_STORE_THREADS` > 8 for that reason.
- **Router lookahead into the store** (`DS4_AHEAD=1`, A/B/A, environment of the test process only):

  | Run | Repeated prompts | Fresh prompts |
  |---|---|---|
  | A1 | 25.0 tok/s | 15.1 tok/s |
  | `DS4_AHEAD=1` | 22.5 tok/s | 14.8 tok/s |
  | A2 | 24.9 tok/s | 16.2 tok/s |

  - It reads 20–25% more from disk.
  - Outputs are identical: the text hash matched for all 13 requests in the three runs.
  - This matches your note in `init_store()` ("measured 4.5 against 4.7 tok/s… DS4_AHEAD=1 turns them on"). Keeping it off is right here too.

## Question
On a miss, the decode path seems to wait on the store reads of a layer about one at a time: queue 0.26–0.38 while the drive can sustain 4–6 GB/s at queue about 2.

1. Could the misses of a layer (and/or the 1 MB pieces of one expert) be issued together, so the NVMe queue fills while the CPU lane waits?
2. Is the per-layer dependency the hard limit, so that only better guesses (lookahead) can hide it?
3. Are the `st.ahead_*` counters (ahead_pf, ahead_hit…) exposed anywhere (log or /metrics)? I could not find where they are printed.

I can rerun any of this with a build or a flag you suggest and post the numbers.
